_comment: The contract between the pipeline and index.html, in one place.
`blocks` names every <script id="..."> block the page reads, the window.* global it
assigns, and the ConvertTo-Json depth its payload needs. Both languages that splice the
page read this file: lib/pagedata.ps1 (daily run) and server/pagedata.py (per request).
Before this file existed the same convention was hand-copied into nine places; a marker
rename silently produced a page with a stale block instead of an error.
`noteFields` is the privacy policy for AI-written per-code notes. `guest` may be published
or shown to non-owners; `ownerOnly` is advice written with the owner's whole portfolio in
view and must never leave this machine. build-demo.ps1 filters to `guest`, the publication
gate refuses on `ownerOnly`, and server/payload.py applies both.
The three guest fields ARE the analysis: technicals, institutional flow, fundamentals, each
confined to its own evidence. They may not reference the index, US markets, the overnight
session or any other holding - that material lives in the market block below and is read
separately, so a per-stock read cannot quietly become a market call. `sigFund` used to sit
here too; the direction chip is computed by lib/score.ps1's Get-FundSignal now, like the
technical and chip chips always were, leaving the AI only the prose.
`marketFields` is the same policy for the market block (window.MARKET, written to
market-notes.json). It used to be a pseudo-code `_market` inside the per-code notes, which
is what let a stock's `fund` paragraph wander off into index commentary. `wind` is ownerOnly
- the daily prompt writes it as commentary on the owner's portfolio ('投組今日明顯分化：
00990A…'), so it names real holdings; buildWind() renders fine from windLead alone. `night`
(the overnight read: what tonight's US session could do to tomorrow's open, and what to do
if it does) is ownerOnly for the same reason - it is written as 若X則Y against this
portfolio's own levels, which is advice, not a market fact. Allowlist, not blocklist: a
field added upstream stays private until it is named here.
One narrower exception, live server only (build-demo.ps1/publish-gate.ps1 are unaffected -
the git-published demo has no guest_plus accounts, so `rec` there is still unconditionally
ownerOnly): a guest_plus grant (server/auth.set_tier) buys a per-account budget of EXTRA
codes (payload.guest_plus_codes_in_budget) that get Claude-quality, portfolio-blind notes
instead of Gemini's, including a rec - safe because the daily prompt writes those codes
with no portfolio in view at all, unlike the owner's own rec. server/payload.py's
notes_for() tells the two apart by code (is it one of the owner's own holdings?), not by
the reader's tier, so this list stays the source of truth for `rec`'s ownerOnly-ness only
as it applies to the owner's OWN codes.
